title: William H. Crawford to James Monroe, Paris, 5 Nov 1814 (Despatch No. 33-2, Private): a coded letter in WE025

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to France vol. 15, M34 roll 18 (naId 188673229), frames 0063R-0067L; code on 0064R, 0065R, 0066L

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the film (frames 0059-0070 checked); 0067R is the last page of a clerk's clear fair copy, the rest of which is not on this roll. Not found in Founders Online, American State Papers FR 3, the Library of Congress Monroe Papers (1902 calendar), Mooney (1974), Willson (1928), Shipp (1909), Cryptiana, or HathiTrust and Google Books phrase searches (NOTES.md section 5).

transcription.source: NARA M34 roll 18 frames 0064-0066 (full resolution, 4960 px wide)
transcription.notes: Two transcriptions made blind of each other by two AI agents (14-15 Nov 2026): 291 of 292 groups the same; the one difference (66L13 307/317) settled on the image as 307. Two groups struck through by Crawford are left out. Measured with docs/_check_profile.py --measure --digits --drop-first.

system.summary: The State Department's numerical code of about 1,600 words and syllables that Weber (1979) prints as WE025 (the = 1355, of = 1397, to = 1554), Poinsett's 'code 1355'; marks on the groups for -s, -ed, dropped and doubled letters.
system.sibling_key: WE025 as printed by Weber 1979 pp. 470-480, in the transcription frozen for ../poinsett1813/beling (sha256 26dad03e...); the 156 rows used here in key/we025_crawford1814.tsv
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct numbers in crawford1814_transcription.txt (python docs/_check_profile.py --measure ... --digits --drop-first). Words in clear are written in among the groups. Marks: diamond above (-s), caret (-ed), r-strokes under (drop final letters), cross under (doubled letter).

prior_solution.where: Monroe's office presumably deciphered it in 1814-15, but no decipherment was found: none on the film (frames 0059-0070), none in the print and online sources listed in NOTES.md section 5. Mooney (1974) cites the letter on the Decatur only. Not seen: the clerk's fair copy (only its last page, 0067R, is on the roll), the Crawford papers at the Library of Congress, the Monroe papers at the New York Public Library, Green (1965).

solution.what: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: a text-layer scan of the NARA catalogue's France despatches flagged roll 18 frames 0064-0066 as code runs with no interlinear decipherment (1355 = the); frames fetched at full size.
First reader: 292 groups in two passes on crops, reconciled and frozen by sha256 before the test.
WE025 (our frozen transcription of Weber's table, made for Poinsett's letters) applied unchanged: all 292 groups have a table value and the text reads as English throughout.

Letter-trigram score of the decode against 200 tables made by shuffling WE025's elements, pass mark written first: real -0.909, shuffled mean -1.191, best -1.067, z 5.7, pass. The first run had a table-parsing bug (half the rows lost) and was repaired and rerun once; both outputs kept.

Second reader, given only the images: a blind transcription frozen before opening the first reader's files; 291 of 292 groups the same, the difference settled on the image; its blind decode gives the same text. The shuffle test rerun from the frozen inputs reproduces exactly.

Eleven groups read from the sense where the written number gives another value: 1512 (our) for 1215 (a) four times, 1276 for 1275 (y), 556 for 1556 (e), 361 for 561 (these), 1474 for 1472 (any); 812 decis[ive] and 1244 1116 [troops] not settled. Bracketed in the reading.

Founders Online, ASP FR 3 contents, the 1902 calendar of the Library of Congress Monroe Papers, Mooney 1974, Willson 1928 and Shipp 1909 (search inside), Cryptiana, Weber 1979, HathiTrust and Google Books phrase searches: no printing or decipherment of the coded part found.
Read (crawford1814_reading.md): 281 of 292 groups straight from the table, eleven supplied and bracketed.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 281 tokens, 155 types, en-modern order 4: reading -1.845 per letter; random keys -2.748 (z 6.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.832 (mean -1.845, z -0.0); annealer on the real text -1.785. Verdict: underdetermined.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.845; polyphony 0.0; 11 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.785

texts.label: Crawford to Monroe, Paris, 5 Nov 1814 (Despatch No. 33-2, Private), M34 roll 18 frames 0064R-0066L
texts.summary: Crawford reports to Monroe, in code, his belief that the French government has resolved to sacrifice everything for England's friendship and that the King looks to British troops in Belgium for protection against his own people; a reported conspiracy headed by Savary, which opponents call a police fabrication to justify about thirty arrests; a coming crisis for the King, with many expecting the royal family to be expelled again; and three parties if there is a struggle: the army for the Emperor, part of the new nobility for the King of Rome with a regency or for the Duke of Orleans, and the republicans with either of the last two.
texts.note: read_share = 281 of 292 groups read from the table value as written.
